source.source: HYG v4.4 (Hipparcos-Yale-Gliese Database, D. Nash / astronexus)
source.epoch: ICRS/J2000 equinox; source astrometry primarily Hipparcos-2007 reduction, epoch J1991.25
source.sentinelDistDoc: dist == 100000.0 marks an unmeasurable/negative Hipparcos parallax; rows with it are dropped, not shipped.
source.hipSentinelDoc: hip == 0 means the row has no Hipparcos catalogue number.

galacticFrame.source: Hipparcos Catalogue vol. 1 §1.5.3 (ESA SP-1200, 1997); J2000 galactic frame constants shared by astropy and SOFA

panorama.title: The Milky Way panorama
panorama.longitudeConvention: l = 0 at the column centre, increasing leftward (sky seen from inside)
panorama.latitudeConvention: b = +90 at row 0, -90 at the last row

catalogRegistration.role: retained source record only; the photograph is registered astrometrically and owns visible stars

pointSourcePresentation.positionSource: licensed ESO photographic local maxima; no Google catalogue bytes
pointSourcePresentation.qualification: native fixed-size catalogue behavior collapsed into the prepared cubemap; point positions and colors remain ESO-derived

sky.qualification: source-photographed full sky sampled in ICRF through the J2000 galactic frame and the anchor-registered panorama; the scene registration carries the Iapetus pole and epoch; Solar System objects in the mosaic are capture artefacts; no Sun is baked into the cubemap
sky.sceneRegistrationChain: galactic -> ICRF (J2000 constants) -> body-fixed (IAU pole and prime meridian at the epoch) -> ecliptic presentation frame

analyticRadialFit.qualification: Least-squares fit to annular red-channel means from the bound native 128 by 128 Sun texture; fitted values only, no source pixels.

distanceScaling.qualification: The opaque photospheric core is projected from the IAU nominal solar radius and the object catalog's mean heliocentric distance. The retained glow profile remains a visual presentation; the distance is not epoch-specific.

provenance.source: JPL Iapetus orbit plus VSOP87 Saturn position and IAU/WGCCRE Iapetus rotation
provenance.qualification: Observed Iapetus Sun direction at 2026-09-04T00:00:00 TT, expressed in the ecliptic presentation frame (north up, Sun left at zero yaw) and in view space at the default camera pose.

controls.label: Monochrome
controls.description: USGS May 2008 Cassini/Voyager mosaic at 803 m per source pixel (5760 × 2880), resampled into the shared texture layout. No additional detail is created. Coarse polar coverage, source seams and photographed shading remain; gray grid marks explicit no-data. Shared Shadows adds approximate globe lighting. Mean-radius sphere: the real equatorial ridge does not change the silhouette.
controls.summary: Polar detail is coarse compared with the rest of the surface. Photographed shadows and seams remain; the grid marks gaps.
controls.title: Multi-mission image mosaic

controls.label: Enhanced color
controls.description: Published 2014 enhanced-color Cassini composite, photometrically corrected by Paul Schenk, with nominal 400 m source pixels. Colors extend into ultraviolet and infrared. The dark leading hemisphere is real surface albedo, not a shadow or missing imagery. All supplied pixels are preserved; coarse patches and residual photographed shading remain. Shared Shadows and globe lighting remain active; shape is approximated by a sphere.
controls.summary: Colors extend into infrared and ultraviolet. The dark leading hemisphere is real surface material, not missing imagery.
controls.title: Enhanced-color composite

controls.label: Infrared
controls.description: Three Cassini VIMS observations from 10 September 2007. False color assigns red to about 2.02 µm, green to 1.59 µm and blue to 1.28 µm. All three channels share a 0–0.45 I/F display range and gamma 2.2; this stretch changes the display only. No photometric correction is applied, so illumination remains. Archive noise filtering and local replacement are retained; original detector defects and potentially affected neighbors are excluded. Gray grid marks unsupported areas and scan gaps.
controls.summary: Cassini false color: red 2.02, green 1.59, blue 1.28 µm. Coverage is partial; gray grid marks gaps. Illumination and archive filtering remain in these uncorrected measurements.
controls.title: Cassini VIMS flyby spectra · 10 September 2007

controls.label: Ice absorption
controls.description: Near-2.02 µm water-ice band depth relative to a linear 1.82–2.20 µm continuum, using three Cassini VIMS observations from 10 September 2007. This measures absorption strength, not ice abundance. Viewing angle, grain size and noise also affect the values; no photometric correction is applied. Archive noise filtering and local replacement remain; original detector defects and potentially affected neighbors are excluded. Display colors saturate outside 0–0.8; original numerical values are retained. Gray grid marks unsupported areas and scan gaps.
controls.summary: Near-2.02 µm water-ice absorption in partial Cassini coverage. Gray grid marks gaps. Viewing angle, grain size, noise and archive filtering affect these uncorrected values; they do not measure ice abundance.
controls.title: Cassini VIMS flyby water-ice absorption · 10 September 2007
